reasoning: AI language models, starting with OpenAI's GPT-4, have successfully passed the Uniform Bar Examination (UBE) with scores that are both above the passing threshold and above the average for human test-takers. In a peer-reviewed study published in 2023 ("GPT-4 Passes the Bar Exam" by Katz et al.), GPT-4 scored 297 out of 400 on a practice administration of the UBE. This score comfortably exceeds the passing score required in any U.S. jurisdiction (which ranges from 260 to 270). The authors originally estimated this score placed GPT-4 in the 90th percentile of test-takers. Although a critique by MIT researcher Eric Martinez argued this percentile was inflated by comparing it to historical February test-takers (who generally score lower than July test-takers) and suggested the true placement was closer to the 68th percentile, both analyses agree that the model comfortably passed and achieved an above-average score. Subsequent frontier LLMs have matched or exceeded these benchmarks.
title: AI systems now pass the bar exam
